Zelensky Launches Direct Talks With Mayors on Winter Grid Defense — President Volodymyr Zelensky convened his first meeting in a new regular format with Ukrainian mayors and local self-government representatives on Friday, Nov. 13, focusing on winter preparedness, energy infrastructure defense, and municipal budget capacity. Zelensky demanded accurate, real-time reporting from local officials after criticizing multi-day blackouts and misleading reports in Bila Tserkva and Brovary.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 13, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 13, 2026.

Azerbaijan Omits Ukraine Drone Deal from Dublin Readout — Ukraine and Azerbaijan issued contrasting accounts of the Nov. 12 meeting between Presidents Volodymyr Zelensky and Ilham Aliyev in Dublin. Kyiv highlighted signed drone contracts and plans to expand orders, while Baku made no mention of military ties. The omission comes as Azerbaijan renews military-technical cooperation with Russia and signals plans to resume gas purchases from Gazprom.

Le Pen Offers to Meet Zelensky in Brussels After Threatening to Cut Ukraine Aid if Elected — French far-right leader Marine Le Pen said she is prepared to meet President Volodymyr Zelensky in Brussels, weeks after threatening to end French financial assistance to Kyiv if elected president in 2027. Le Pen said the meeting would be appropriate given Europe’s debate over Ukraine funding.

US Senators Demand Musk Preserve Records on Ukraine’s Starlink Access, Set Nov. 30 Deadline — Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons demanded that Elon Musk preserve SpaceX records concerning restrictions on Ukraine’s Starlink and Starshield systems, setting a Nov. 30 deadline for confirmation. Separately, Congressmen Gregory Meeks and Adam Smith warned that the restrictions contributed to Ukrainian civilian deaths, including children, and strengthened Vladimir Putin’s negotiating position.

Trump to Meet Putin and Xi in China, But Won’t Discuss Russia’s War in Ukraine, White House Says — US President Donald Trump will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 19. The White House said discussions will focus on nuclear arms reduction and Iran, while Russia’s war against Ukraine will remain off the agenda.

‘Problems Must Be Solved, Not Hidden’: Zelensky Slams Officials Over Days-Long Blackouts as Ukraine Faces Harsh Winter — President Volodymyr Zelensky sharply criticized Ukrainian officials over prolonged electricity outages in Bila Tserkva and Brovary, where residents went days without power despite misleading reports from local authorities. His warning came as DTEK chief executive Maxim Timchenko warned that Russia’s intensified missile and drone attacks could cause far greater damage to Ukrain

Zelensky Says Starshield Restrictions Remain as 105 US Congressmen Demand Ukraine’s Access Be Restored — President Volodymyr Zelensky said US-operated Starshield restrictions remain in place, limiting Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones. The bipartisan Congressional Ukraine Caucus, speaking on behalf of 105 House members, demanded that the Trump administration and SpaceX explain the disruptions and restore full access. Two US senators also called for congressional oversight, while Spac

‘I Know the Russians Don’t Want Me’: Kallas Warns Europe Against Putin’s Trap in Ukraine Peace Talks — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned Europe against falling into Russia’s negotiating trap by discussing Moscow’s security demands before securing a ceasefire in Ukraine. She rejected Russia’s claims of security concerns, called for Europe to present its own maximum demands, and pushed back against Kremlin opposition to her participation in peace negotiations.

Sybiha Urges UN to Prioritize Ukraine’s Power Grid as Zelensky Condemns ‘Unacceptable’ Blackouts — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha urged UN agencies to make restoring Ukraine’s power and heating infrastructure a priority in their life-saving programs, particularly as Russia intensifies strikes on the country’s power grid ahead of winter. The appeal came as President Volodymyr Zelensky called days-long outages in the Kyiv region cities of Bila Tserkva and Brovary “absolutely unacceptable,” saying

Parliament Backs 6 Bills Tied to EU Funds After Months of Stalling — Ukraine’s parliament backed six bills required under the EU’s Ukraine Facility, adopting two in full and four in the first reading, after months of deadlock that lasted until the state treasury ran nearly empty. The EU funding tied to these steps totals about €1.5 billion ($1.7 billion), but Kyiv must complete all legislative procedures and win the European Commission’s approval first.

Europe Settles on Negotiating Team for Russia-Ukraine Talks — National security advisers from the EU and the E5 format – France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK – will represent Europe in upcoming Russia-Ukraine peace talks, Bloomberg reported on Friday, Nov. 13, citing a senior European official. Speaking after an informal meeting in Dublin, European Council President Antonio Costa confirmed that the team would consist of the EU institutions and the E5 of the Coalition of the Willing. They wi

Kernel Halts All Oilseed Crushing Plants After Russian Drone Strikes — Kernel Holding, the world’s largest sunflower oil producer and exporter, has halted all its oilseed crushing plants after Russian drones damaged production buildings, equipment and storage tanks. Russia’s hit on Kernel’s facilities caused a large spill of oil in the Mykolaiv region.

Ukraine’s Health Ministry Drafts Comprehensive Law to Regulate AI in Medicine — Ukraine’s Health Ministry is drafting legislation to regulate artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, Health Minister Viktor Liashko said on Friday, Nov. 13, citing a ministry survey which shows that 80.5% of medical workers already use the technology. The bill would set rules for developing and using medical AI systems, as well as for classifying them by risk level. Safety, transparency and accountability will be
Inside the $5 Trillion Espionage Scandal Rocking Nvidia and Silicon Valley — The CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, is at the center of a major national security story.

Rescuer Among 3 Dead as Russian Strikes Wound 50 in Zaporizhzhia — Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia on Friday, Nov. 13 killed two people and injured 50, including eight children. A five-story residential building was hit in the Kosmichnyi district, while a separate strike killed a 17-year-old boy. A member of the Kobra rescue service also died after a concrete slab fell on him while he was clearing rubble. A woman injured on Thursday, Nov. 11, also died in hospital on Friday.

Ukraine Downs Russian Geran-5 Drone With Swedish RBS-70 in Kyiv Region for First Time — Ukraine’s Defense Forces shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran-5 drone over the Kyiv region, using a Swedish RBS-70 man-portable air defense system (MANPADS) for the first time, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) said on Friday, Nov. 13. The interception was made by the 1027th Anti-Aircraft Missile and Artillery Regiment. Russia’s growing use of jet-powered drones, which can reach speeds o

China Rehearses Taiwan Strikes Ahead of APEC Summit — China simulated attacks on Taiwanese cities during unannounced military drills, a senior Taiwanese security official told Reuters. More than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard vessels have been reported across the wider region. The activity comes ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, where Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet, with a possible Putin meeting also under discussion.

Who Speaks for Europe? That Depends on How Tough It Wants to Be on Russia — Europe wants a voice in Ukraine peace talks but remains divided over who should speak. The debate over António Costa and Kaja Kallas revives an older struggle between Baltic warnings about Moscow and Western Europe’s preference for familiar consensus-builders.

Russian Attacks Destroy Acres of Warehouse Space in Ukraine — Russian attacks damaged 153 Ukrainian warehouse facilities between July and September, contributing to 2.1 million square meters in total storage losses since 2022. The National Bank of Ukraine reports this destruction has pushed up both premium warehouse lease rates and inflation.

Merz Says Germany ‘Guaranteed’ a Seat at Ukraine Peace Talks — Merz said on Friday that Germany would join upcoming negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine, as US and Ukrainian officials confirmed plans for another meeting involving Europe. The German chancellor also cautioned Washington against a “second Anchorage moment” and alignment with Moscow.

Zelensky Slams Slow Energy Repairs Amid Growing Russian Strikes — The Ukrainian leader has criticized slow repairs following Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, citing major problems in Sumy and Kyiv regions. He said several cities had provided inaccurate information about restoration progress and asked three ministers to improve coordination with local authorities. The remarks come amid an ongoing Russian campaign against substations and power facilities that led to nationwide b

French Envoy Calls Russia’s Security Demand ‘Legitimate’ — France’s ambassador to Russia, Nicolas de Rivière, said Moscow’s request for security guarantees was legitimate, while stressing that Ukraine also needed protection. In an RTVI interview, he called for a ceasefire and European involvement in shaping a settlement. His remarks came as Ukraine warned that talks on guarantees could expand into a broader security arrangement between Europe and Russia.

Kyiv Forum to Tackle Ukraine’s Wartime Democracy, EU Reforms and Role of Veterans — The Nov. 17 forum in Kyiv will bring together government officials, diplomats, veterans, young people and media representatives to discuss strengthening democracy during the war. Three panels will focus on EU integration, civic participation and independent media.

Ukraine’s Neptune Missiles Hit Drone Plant, Warehouse, Repair Center in Russia's Rostov — Ukraine's General Staff said the Navy's Neptune coastal missile system struck three drone-related sites in Rostov-on-Don, southern Russia, overnight on 13 Nov.. It is the latest in a series of Neptune strikes on Russian military-industrial targets, after Marinovka airfield on 29 Oct. and the Proton-Elektroteks plant in Oryol on 7 Nov.. The claims have not been independently confirmed.

Russia Destroyed 400 Ukrainian Locomotives in 2026, Infrastructure Minister Says — Ukraine has lost nearly 400 locomotives to Russian attacks in 2026, bringing the total to 630 since Russia’s 2022 invasion began, Infrastructure Minister Mykola Kalashnyk said. With attacks intensifying and replacement equipment in short supply, Kyiv is seeking international help, including used locomotives and spare parts, to keep the trains moving.

Starshield Missions Face 100% Failure Rate in Ukraine – Axios — Ukraine says renewed Starshield speed restrictions are preventing its interceptors from pursuing Russian jet-powered drones. President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking answers from Washington, while US senators have demanded that service be restored and responsibility established. SpaceX denies making changes to the system, which suffered a similar interruption in October before service was restored.

Jan De Winne: The Lost Sounds of Classical Music and His Return to Kyiv — Belgian flautist and historical instrument maker Jan De Winne discusses Mozart, period instruments, musical listening, and his decision to return to Kyiv during wartime to perform and teach young Ukrainian musicians.

EXPLAINED: Tsikhanouski Helped Make His Wife Belarus’ Opposition Leader – Now Wants Her Job — Siarhei Tsikhanouski, the Belarusian opposition figure who helped spark the 2020 protests and brought his wife Sviatlana into politics, has returned from five years in prison to find her leading the country’s democratic opposition. Now based in the US, he has launched a public campaign against her leadership, questioning her legitimacy, attacking her advisers, and accusing her team of neglecting him. As

Russia's Demands for Ukraine Go Beyond Donbas — Russia's reported proposals include taking all of Donbas, demilitarizing Ukrainian ports, forcing Finland out of NATO, and removing Alliance bases from the Baltic states. The informal plan also outlines changes to Moldova and Belarus, BILD reports.

FSB Says It Foiled Plot to Bomb Stavropol Shopping Mall — The FSB said it arrested a man suspected of preparing an attack on a shopping mall in Stavropol for an unnamed terrorist organization. The agency released interrogation footage, but its account has not been independently verified.

Kremlin-Seized Foreign Firms Channel Billions Into Putin’s War Chest — Russian branches of foreign firms placed under Kremlin-backed management have channeled billions of rubles towards Russia’s military, Bloomberg reported. The donations have funded drones, vehicles and communications equipment through a Putin-founded organization. Companies affected include Rockwool, AkzoNobel, DKC Europe, Metro and AB InBev Efes, while their international parent companies have lost operational control of thei

Russia’s Starlink Rival Lags Behind Plans, Kyiv Says — Russia’s Rassvet satellites remain below their planned orbital altitude, Ukraine’s military intelligence said, while Moscow prepares more spacecraft and terminal models. Air Assault Forces commander Oleh Apostol said Russia could eventually overcome its technological difficulties, although development was taking longer than planned. The network already provides intermittent military communications over Ukraine, according to intelligence offi

SBU General Posts Full $1.5M Bail in Ukraine Criminal Network Case — SBU Major General Serhiy Duka, suspected of helping an organized criminal network buy protection from Ukrainian law enforcement, has had UAH 65 million ($1.5 million) in bail posted in the Operation Carthage case. The investigation implicates officials from the SBU, National Police, and Prosecutor General’s Office in an alleged scheme involving bribes, drug trafficking, fraudulent call centers, and other illegal businesses.

Romania Offers to Help Pay for Larger US Military Presence — Romania is seeking a stronger US military presence through a cost-sharing proposal modeled on Poland’s arrangement. The offer comes as Washington reviews its European deployments, a year after reducing troop numbers in Romania.

Russian Drone Attack Damages Kyiv Trauma Institute — Russia launched a major drone assault on Ukraine overnight on Friday, damaging Kyiv’s trauma institute and striking residential neighborhoods in several regions. The attacks killed civilians, including a teenager, and injured adults and children. Kyiv recently warned that Starshield disruptions have hampered Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones.

Moscow Car Blast Reportedly Injures Former Azarov Spokesman — A Toyota Fortuner exploded in southern Moscow on Friday, reportedly seriously injuring Sergei Zavorotny, a Russian writer who previously worked for former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov.

Russian Strikes Kill 2 Women in Odesa, Injure 6 Others — Russian strikes on Odesa on Nov. 13 killed two women and injured six people, according to a regional prosecutor’s spokeswoman, updating an earlier toll of five injured. All six were hospitalized, as private homes and cars were damaged during successive morning attacks, and emergency crews were deployed to the affected locations.

Russian Advance Loses ‘Significant’ Momentum, Ukraine’s Air Assault Chief Says — Ukraine’s Air Assault Forces Commander Apostol said Russia’s advance has slowed significantly, partly due to heavy losses. He adds that capturing isolated positions does not amount to meaningful operational success, while acknowledging Moscow’s manpower advantage.

Finland, Norway Block Visas for Russian Athletes — Finland will deny short-term work visas to Russian athletes, including those competing under a neutral flag, from Nov. 16, while Norway is also tightening entry restrictions. The moves could affect major international competitions, including the 2027 Figure Skating World Championships in Tampere and upcoming skiing and ice hockey tournaments.

Russia Scraps Army 2027 Weapons Expo as Kremlin Scales Back Military Showpieces — Russia has canceled its flagship Army 2027 military-technical forum for the third consecutive year, scrapping a major international weapons exhibition that once showcased the country’s military-industrial might. The decision follows earlier cancellations in 2025 and 2026, as the Kremlin scales back the event, which was also a lucrative business for a company linked to former Defense Minister Sergey Shoigu’s family.

Ukraine Talks: Is Peace Any Closer? — European media express concern over Europe’s exclusion from US-brokered Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi. Commentators question Europe’s diplomatic influence, warn that Putin may not honour a ceasefire, and fear a cynical settlement that undermines Ukraine’s sovereignty and European security. Others call for stronger European diplomacy and a broader security framework involving Russia, Ukraine, NATO and Western allies.

Ukraine Confirms Volgograd Refinery Strike as Russia Claims 1,198 Drones Downed in Massive Overnight Attack — Ukraine struck the Lukoil-owned Volgograd refinery again, triggering a fire, killing four workers and raising fresh concerns over fuel supplies as Russian oil processing capacity continues to shrink under repeated drone attacks.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 12, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 12, 2026.

Putin Threatens European Troops, Revives 2021 Ultimatums to Roll Back NATO — Russian President Vladimir Putin warned on Thursday, Nov. 12, that European troops deployed to Ukraine after a peace agreement would become legitimate military targets. Following his meeting with US envoys in Moscow, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reported that Russia remained unwilling to compromise on its territorial demands and had revived its 2021 ultimatums to restrict NATO’s presence in Eastern Europe.

US Senators Demand Starshield Restoration as Kyiv Reports Renewed Disruptions — US Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Thom Tillis demanded on Thursday, Nov. 12, that the Trump administration and SpaceX immediately restore Ukraine’s Starshield satellite communications capabilities following reports of renewed restrictions. The bipartisan lawmakers called for congressional oversight, warning that disruptions were weakening Ukraine’s defenses against Russian drones. Zelensky also raised the issue with NAT

Finland, Norway Move to Ban Russian Athletes Over Ukraine War — Finland and Norway announced new restrictions on Thursday, Nov. 12, aimed at preventing Russian athletes from competing in international sporting events on their territory while Moscow continues its war against Ukraine. Norway’s measures also target Belarusian professional athletes and support staff. The decisions could affect major skiing and figure skating competitions despite international sports federations allowing some Russian

Russian Attack Damages Kindergarten and Homes in Vinnytsia, Injures 2 — A Russian overnight attack on Vinnytsia early on Friday, Nov. 13, injured two women and damaged a kindergarten, private homes, and apartment buildings, according to Mayor Serhiy Morhunov. Both women were hospitalized, while emergency services responded to a residential fire and assessed the damage.

Russian Drones Target Kyiv Overnight, Debris Ignites Medical Facility — Russian drones attacked Kyiv overnight on Friday, Nov. 13, with falling debris sparking a fire at a medical facility in the Shevchenkivskyi district, according to the Kyiv City Military Administration. Emergency services responded as air raid alerts sounded across the capital.

Europe to Join Next Ukraine Peace Talks Following US-Putin Meeting — European representatives will participate in the next round of Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations, President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff said Thursday, Nov. 12, following talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Zelensky said the agenda would include ceasefires and de-escalation measures, alongside a major prisoner-of-war exchange agreement.

Merz Cites E3, Five-Nation Formats as Options for Europe in Talks With Russia — Speaking to reporters in Ireland on Thursday, Nov. 12, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that he would have no problem with Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland representing Europe in future peace talks with Russia. Although no final decision has been made yet, Merz said securing Russia’s agreement to joint negotiations matters more than naming representatives. During the same 9th European Political Communit

UK Becomes First Country to Blacklist Russia’s 10 Biggest Oil Producers — The UK sanctioned all 10 of Russia’s largest oil producers on Thursday, Nov. 12, becoming the first country to do so. The new package includes Slavneft, Rosneft’s Vostok Oil project, as well as coal companies and shadow fleet vessels used to bypass Western sanctions. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the move at the 9th European Political Community (EPC) summit in Dublin, where he and President Volodymyr Zelens

Russian Drones Hit One of Ukraine's Oldest Oil Extraction Plants — A Nov. 10 Russian drones strike critically damaged the Nizhyn Fat and Oil Plant, a historic civilian facility in the Chernihiv region. The incident marks over 100 attacks on agricultural enterprises across the region since the start of 2026

New Round of Ukraine Talks Set, European Representatives to Participate — A new round of trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US has been scheduled, with European leaders included. Speaking to media after a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, Nov. 12, senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner confirmed multilateral talks will take place as early as next week. Neither envoy, however, provided an exact date or venue, while Kremlin aide Yuri

Trump, Putin to Meet at APEC in China as Europe Seeks Seat at Ukraine Talks — Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump plan to meet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19 to continue discussing the war in Ukraine, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said on Thursday, Nov. 12. According to Ushakov, work is underway on a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The announcement followed Putin’s talks with US envoys Steve Wi

Zelensky Questions US-Russia Push for New Security Model With Europe — Speaking at the 9th European Political Community (EPC) Summit in Dublin on Thursday, Nov. 12, President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed that the US-Russia talks on security are less about guarantees for Ukraine, and more about a new security model between Europe and Russia. He called the approach “somewhat strange,” noting that Europe sought close ties with Moscow for three decades after the Soviet collapse. During the same summit

Ukrainian Soldier’s Online Dating Ends in Murder Plot Arrest — The Security Service of Ukraine said it detained a mobilized paratrooper in Mykolaiv suspected of helping Russia’s FSB prepare a missile strike to kill his brigade commander. Investigators say the man attracted Russian intelligence attention while seeking relationships on Telegram dating channels, then collected targeting information for a handler. He is being held without bail on suspicion of wartime treason and faces life imprisonm

Kremlin Suppresses Photos of Military Graves as War Deaths Multiply — Russian authorities are tightening restrictions on documenting soldiers’ graves, increasingly treating cemetery photography as a national security offense. The crackdown comes as independent journalists and researchers continue to uncover mounting military deaths in Ukraine despite classified records, restricted statistics and threats of prosecution. Independent databases suggest confirmed deaths represent only a fraction of R

Ukraine’s Lima System Diverted 2 Russian Oreshnik Missiles — Ukraine’s Lima system diverted two Russian Oreshnik ballistic missiles fired toward the Kyiv region on May 24, Ukrainian soldiers told The New York Times. The system interferes with satellite navigation to misdirect incoming weapons, but also disrupts civilian GPS devices, sometimes placing users thousands of miles away in Peru.

Zelensky: Putin Wants to ‘Destroy Life’ in Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian President Vladimir Putin told people in his inner circle he wanted to “destroy life” in Ukrainian cities, urging European partners to help implement winter resilience plans. Speaking at the European Political Community summit in Dublin on Thursday, Nov. 12, Zelensky said plans were ready for Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, and other cities but needed “special support.”

Ukraine to Get Advanced Czech Trainer Jet to Fight Russian Drones — Czechia plans to transfer 16 L-39 Skyfox jets to Ukraine for anti-drone defense. Four already agreed, 12 more preliminary. Aero’s Drone Hunter variant (70mm guided rockets, EO targeting) is in development. Recent Russian strike launched 123+ drones/missiles; Ukraine claimed 94 downed.

Ukraine Reports Long-Range Strikes on Russia’s 5 Largest Oil Refineries — Ukraine has struck at least nine Russian oil refineries between Oct. 30 and Nov. 11, including five of the country’s largest facilities, Ukraine’s General Staff said. The targeted plants have a combined nominal capacity exceeding 120 million metric tons annually, or around 36% of Russia’s total.

Kyiv Ping-Pong: Who’s Really to Blame for the Capital’s Blackouts? — Intensified Russian strikes have pushed Kyiv to the brink of a municipal crisis, exposing years of neglect – too few shelters, crumbling bridges, chaotic transport and a water utility without backup power. But much lies beyond City Hall’s reach: the capital now absorbs nearly 40% of Russia’s missiles, and its power sources sit outside city limits. The feud between Mayor Vitali Klitschko and President Volodymyr Zelensky’s office

Witkoff Floats European Role in Next Ukraine Peace Talks After Abu Dhabi Sidelined EU — Witkoff signaled that Europe could join the next round of Ukraine peace talks after being sidelined in Abu Dhabi, where US, Ukrainian, and Russian officials negotiated without European representatives. Moscow has resisted European involvement, while Washington is discussing the continent’s future security arrangements with its allies.

Black Sea Becomes World’s Deadliest Shipping Route — More than 300 attacks in the Black Sea this year have killed over 30 seafarers and left more than 20 missing, making it the world’s deadliest shipping route. Russian strikes on Ukrainian export vessels and Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian shipping have disrupted trade, with recent attacks spreading toward Romania and Bulgaria.

Ukraine Strikes Omsk Oil Refinery for Third Time, SSO Says — Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces (SSO) said its Deep Strike units struck the Omsk Oil Refinery on Nov. 11, marking the third attack on Russia’s largest refinery since July. The plant, owned by Gazprom Neft and located about 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from Ukraine, processes more than 21 million metric tons of oil annually and supplies Russia’s military, according to Ukraine’s General Staff.

Russia Praises NATO Commander’s Role in Ukraine Talks — Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov praised General Alexus Grynkewich’s contribution to the Abu Dhabi talks while warning against European participation in future negotiations. Grynkewich, NATO’s top commander in Europe, attended in his US military capacity. The comments came as Washington sought a broader negotiating format and prepared further talks with Vladimir Putin.

Putin’s ‘Permanent Peace’ Pitch Comes With New Demands for Ukraine — Putin proposed another humanitarian mission in Ukraine, this time from Kostyantynivka, while claiming Russian control of the city and calling for “permanent peace.” US envoys Witkoff and Kushner also discussed POW exchanges and Europe’s future security role.

St. Petersburg Blast Took Out Russian Officers Protecting Airspace From Arctic to Kaliningrad — Ukrainian monitoring channels have named three colonels from Russia’s 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army as possible victims of the Thursday car bombing in St. Petersburg. The officers reportedly held senior command positions in a military structure responsible for protecting Russian airspace across the northwest. Russian media say a 31-year-old suspect allegedly planted the bomb before fleeing to Mol

Did Russia Shoot Down Its Own Helicopters While Repelling Ukrainian Drone Attack? — Milbloggers and mainstream media have reported that as Russia tried to repel Ukraine’s drone attacks on the Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga overnight into Wednesday morning, air defenses brought down three Russian helicopters. There has been no official confirmation from Moscow’s Defense Ministry.

Russia Bans Ukrainian Resistance Movement Yellow Ribbon, Labels It ‘Extremist’ — Russia’s Supreme Court has designated Yellow Ribbon, a Ukrainian resistance movement, as an extremist organization and banned its activities in Russia. The court held proceedings behind closed doors and accused the group of operating under Ukrainian intelligence supervision with foreign funding. Founded in occupied Kherson in April 2022, Yellow Ribbon became known for peaceful acts of resistance against Russian occu

South Korea Keeps Ukraine Aid Flowing Despite Dispute Over POWs — South Korea is pushing ahead with $100 million in planned aid for Ukraine despite a diplomatic row over Kyiv’s transfer of two North Korean POWs to Seoul, which prompted Seoul to recall its ambassador and withdraw embassy staff. A first meeting between the two countries’ foreign ministers since the fallout signals a possible reset in relations, as North Korea deepens its military role in Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Ukraine's Drone Interceptors Hampered by Starshield Speed Cap — Zelensky said Starshield's 161 kph speed restriction is hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and has contributed to successful strikes. Ukraine is seeking an explanation from the US following a massive overnight Russian attack.

FSB Detains 4 Alleged Ukrainian Agents in 3 Separate Incidents — The FSB said on Thursday it detained four individuals, one a foreign national, in the Republic of Adygea, the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic and the Omsk Region. It accused them of working for Ukrainian intelligence and said it had recovered an IED and a grenade in Donetsk.

Russia’s War Demands Go Far Beyond Donbas, ISW Warns — Russia’s demands after the Abu Dhabi talks show no retreat from its pursuit of Ukrainian capitulation, according to the Institute for the Study of War. Moscow is demanding territory beyond Donbas, rejecting land swaps, and repeating calls for Ukraine to abandon NATO membership, while using exaggerated battlefield claims to strengthen its negotiating position, the analysts said.

RAND Scenario: Putin Dies in 3 Months, Russia Attacks NATO by 2030 in Hypothetical War Plan — RAND outlines a hypothetical chain of events in which Putin’s death leads to a new Russian leadership, a frozen war in Ukraine and escalating hybrid attacks against NATO. By 2030, Moscow launches an incursion into Estonia, triggering a wider war with the alliance. The scenario ends in 2031 with a ceasefire, Russian forces occupying parts of Estonia and NATO’s credibility undermined.

Russian Ambassador to US Dies: Foreign Ministry — Russia’s ambassador to the US Darchiev has died in Moscow at age 66, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced. Appointed in March 2025, he previously served as ambassador to Canada and headed the ministry’s North America department.

Ukraine to Allocate $43M for 113 Reconstruction Projects Amid Ongoing War — Kyiv has allocated an additional Hr.1.8 billion ($43 million) to finance 113 infrastructure projects nationwide. The funding will prioritize schools, hospitals, rehabilitation facilities, water supplies and energy efficiency measures. Prime Minister Kotetskyi said local communities had selected the projects based on their most pressing needs.

Merz Could Speak With Putin After Abu Dhabi Peace Talks — Berlin says contacts between Merz and Putin could follow the Abu Dhabi talks, while Moscow says its next steps will depend on briefings to the Russian president.

Music That Survived a Millennium: Sequentia on Memory, War, and Cultural Solidarity — For nearly five decades, Sequentia has explored medieval European music, reconstructing repertoires that were lost to oral tradition. Ahead of Kyiv Baroque Fest 2026, Benjamin Bagby and Norbert Rodenkirchen discuss historical reconstruction, cultural memory, the enduring power of ancient stories, and the meaning of bringing medieval music to Kyiv during Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Russia Loses Vietnam-War-Level Troop Numbers in a Month, Rutte Says — Russia is losing more than 40,000 troops killed or seriously wounded monthly in Ukraine, NATO Secretary Rutte said, adding that preliminary figures suggest October losses may have exceeded 50,000.

1 Killed, 5 Injured as Russian Drone Hits Kyiv Apartment Block — A Russian drone struck a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district on Thursday morning, Nov. 12, injuring two people and causing a fire and structural damage. The strike followed an overnight ballistic missile barrage.

Russian Colonel Blown Up in St. Petersburg as Attacks on Military Figures Mount — A Russian colonel was killed in a car bombing in St. Petersburg’s Slavyanka neighborhood, the second such attack in the area in less than three months. Previous attacks have killed Russian military figures in Sevastopol and near Moscow, while an August explosion at a Moscow restaurant may have targeted Aerospace Forces chief Alexander Chaiko.

As Poland Celebrates Independence, What Holds Ukraine Together? — Poland’s survival through generations without independence offers a lesson for Ukraine. Beyond resistance to Russia, Ukrainians need a shared sense of belonging and reasons to build their future at home.

‘Putin Doesn’t Get to Choose’: Estonia Backs Kallas as EU Peace Envoy — Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal defends Kaja Kallas and António Costa as Europe’s representatives in Ukraine peace negotiations, rejecting concerns that Kallas is too critical of Russia and insisting Moscow must have no say in Europe’s choice.

Russia Pounds Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles, Fires Reported Across Capital — Russia launched an overnight ballistic missile attack on Kyiv early on Thursday, triggering explosions, air raid alerts, and fires across parts of the capital as Ukrainian air defenses responded.

‘Trump and His Envoys Are Working for Putin, Not the US,’ Democrats Warn — Top congressional Democrats sharply condemn Trump, Kushner, and Witkoff for undermining Ukraine, pressuring Kyiv to surrender sovereign territory, and promoting Kremlin demands that threaten NATO and US national security.

Rubio, Wang Discussed Trilateral Summit With Russia, China Makes No Mention — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed high-level diplomacy, including a possible trilateral summit with Russia, as Washington pushes talks on peace and nuclear disarmament.

Zelensky Rules Out Donbas Concessions as Trump Envoys Arrive in Moscow for Talks — As Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin, Zelensky rejects US pressure to surrender Donbas, demands firm security guarantees, and questions Russia’s willingness to compromise.

Ireland Backs Ukraine’s 2027 Funding and Tougher Russia Sanctions — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin pledges to help secure Ukraine’s 2027 funding, backs tougher sanctions on Russia, while Zelensky announces Ireland’s participation in a coalition to build shelters.
